summary: Reviewed 2 files: orchestrator/src/nodes/prompt_renderer.py, orchestrator/tests/test_prompt_renderer.py. 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium, 2 Low (defence-in-depth, noted). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A03/A04 — Defence-in-depth: load_partial(name) and load_template(stage) are public functions that construct file paths via Path(_DIR) / f'{name}.md' with NO validation on the name/stage parameter. A direct caller could pass '../../../etc/passwd' and the pathlib concatenation would produce a path outside the partials directory. Exploitability is negligible: (1) the only call site within render_prompt() is gated by _INCLUDE_RE whose capture group [\w-]+ structurally forbids . and /, and (2) the orchestrator has no external-facing API surface — all callers are internal node factories that pass developer-authored strings. Recommendation: consider adding a guard in load_partial() and load_template() such as 'if not re.fullmatch(r'[\w-]+', name): raise ValueError(...)' to make path-safety invariants explicit and resilient to future callers. File: orchestrator/src/nodes/prompt_renderer.py, lines 95-100 (load_template) and 111-125 (load_partial).

A03 — Informational: render_prompt() uses str.format_map() which in Python supports attribute and item access notation ({var.attr}, {var[key]}). If a template variable's value were itself a complex object, a maliciously crafted template line could potentially read internal attributes. In the current implementation this is not exploitable: (1) all variable values are plain strings (project_path, wp_id, etc.) and (2) templates are developer-authored static .md files in the package directory. Awareness note for when the template corpus grows. File: orchestrator/src/nodes/prompt_renderer.py, line 201.

BLOCKING — orchestrator/tests/test_prompt_renderer.py, TestLoadPartial class: two methods are defined with the same name `test_returns_string`. Python class attribute assignment silently replaces the first definition with the second when the class body is evaluated. Result: (1) the first method (lines ~145-151, which correctly calls `load_partial` and asserts `isinstance(result, str)`) is permanently dropped and never executed; (2) the surviving second method (lines ~175-183) patches `_TEMPLATES_DIR` and calls `load_template()` — it tests the wrong function and carries a wrong docstring ('load_template must return a str, not bytes' inside TestLoadPartial). This second method also properly belongs in TestLoadTemplate, which currently has no str-type assertion for load_template. Required fix: rename the first method to `test_returns_str_not_bytes` (keeping its load_partial body), then either rename the second method distinctly (e.g. `test_load_template_returns_str_not_bytes`) and move it to TestLoadTemplate, or simply remove it from TestLoadPartial and add it to TestLoadTemplate. Both the lost coverage for load_partial and the misplaced coverage for load_template must be restored.
